clips.text_zh: 我喺2024年11月高位將全副身家套入 MSTR。兩年慢慢流乾晒成個net worth。每次細細 pump 都畀我啲希望，翌日又 dump。每次「averaged down」，實際只跌得更慘。我只想攞返啲錢，連 MSTR 帶住 BTC 都跌咗，我真係唔知點算。
clips.text_en_b1: I aped my life savings into MSTR at the top in November 2024. Two years of slowly bleeding out my entire net worth. Every small pump gave me hope, but it dumped the next day. Every time I averaged down, it dropped even more. I just want my money back. I’m down $70,000.
clips.text_en_b2: I aped my entire life savings into MSTR back in November 2024, right near the top, and over the past two years I have watched my net worth slowly bleed out. Every modest pump gave me a flicker of hope, yet it dumped again the following day. Although I kept averaging down, each attempt only made the losses worse. Even with BTC falling alongside MSTR, I simply want my money back. I’m down $70,000.
clips.text_en_c1: I invested my entire life savings in MSTR at the top in November 2024, and over the following two years my net worth slowly bled out. Every modest pump revived my hope, yet the stock dumped the following day. Whenever I averaged down, the position only became more deeply underwater. Now I simply want my money back. Even holding BTC alongside MSTR failed to soften the damage, and at this point I genuinely do not know what to do.
clips.text_en_c2: In November 2024, at the height of the mania, I aped my entire life savings into MSTR. What followed was a slow, two-year haemorrhage of my net worth, punctuated by false dawns that felt all the more convincing because they were so fleeting. Every modest pump revived a flicker of hope, only for the stock to dump the following session. Each time I convinced myself that averaging down was prudent, the position deteriorated even further. I no longer have a strategy; I simply want my money back. Even BTC has fallen alongside MSTR. I am down $70,000, and I genuinely do not know what to do next.
clips.source_hint: An anon describes losing $70,000 after buying MSTR near its November 2024 high and averaging down.

clips.text_zh: 咁我問下，forex trading 真係賺到錢，定係純粹 meme？睇落好似條路好難。靠住 CFD 輸到當學費，邊個仲有正常回報就最好。
clips.text_en_b1: Can you actually make money from forex trading, or is it mostly a meme? Some people treat charts and online signals like real expertise. For me, CFD losses already feel expensive enough. It would be good to hear from anyone with a realistic, repeatable approach.
clips.text_en_b2: So, a genuine question: can you actually make money trading forex, or is it largely a meme? It looks like an incredibly difficult path, especially when people treat chart patterns and online signals as genuine expertise. For me, blowing money on CFDs already feels like paying tuition for a very expensive lesson. It would be reassuring to hear from anyone with a realistic, repeatable approach that produces normal returns instead of fantasy screenshots.
clips.text_en_c1: Can people realistically make money from forex trading, or is the whole thing largely a meme? The charts and online signals that circulate often masquerade as genuine expertise, although the path to consistent returns appears extremely difficult. My own losses through CFDs already feel like an exorbitant tuition fee. If anyone has a realistic, repeatable approach that does not depend on hindsight or luck, I would be interested to hear it.
clips.text_en_c2: Can one actually make money trading forex, or is the entire enterprise a elaborate meme dressed up in technical jargon? Charts, candlesticks and signal groups are routinely treated as expertise, although most participants would struggle to define risk management without resorting to platitudes. Having already paid for my education in life lessons through CFD losses, I am not eager to repeat the experiment. What I would welcome is an account from someone who has achieved consistent, repeatable returns, preferably one that acknowledges the long road, the drawdowns and the unglamorous arithmetic involved. Otherwise, the honest conclusion may be that this is a casino with extra steps.
clips.source_hint: A /biz/ thread asks whether forex trading is profitable or merely a meme.

clips.text_zh: Jensen Huang 據報同盟友討論回歸做 Nvidia CEO。有人話 Silicon Valley 高管正組「war room」，爭取白宮支持。Tesla 同 SpaceX CEO Elon Musk、Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney 都支持公開信。Nvidia 員工嗰邊就更加炸晒，鬧爆要 JENSENNNNNNNN 返嚟。
clips.text_en_b1: Jensen Huang has discussed coming back as Nvidia CEO with his allies. One ally said Silicon Valley executives were forming a “war room” to lobby for his return and White House support. Elon Musk and Tim Sweeney backed a public letter. Nvidia employees also demanded Jensen’s return.
clips.text_en_b2: Jensen Huang has reportedly discussed returning as Nvidia CEO with his allies. One of them claimed that Silicon Valley executives are forming a “war room” to lobby for his comeback and secure White House support. Elon Musk and Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney also backed a public letter demanding his return. Meanwhile, Nvidia employees have gone completely ballistic, spamming messages that simply read “JENSENNNNNNNN.” Even if the whole thing sounds wildly dramatic, the reaction speaks for itself.
clips.text_en_c1: Jensen Huang has reportedly discussed a possible return as Nvidia’s CEO with allies close to him. One supporter claimed that Silicon Valley executives were assembling a “war room” to lobby for his comeback and secure White House backing. Elon Musk, the CEO of Tesla and SpaceX, and Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney also supported a public letter calling for Jensen’s return. Meanwhile, Nvidia employees have been even more vocal, demanding that he come back.
clips.text_en_c2: Jensen Huang is reportedly among the allies with whom he has discussed a potential return as Nvidia CEO. One supporter claimed that Silicon Valley executives were assembling a “war room” to lobby for his reinstatement and to marshal White House support, which suggests that the lobbying effort has acquired considerable institutional weight. Elon Musk, the CEO of Tesla and SpaceX, and Tim Sweeney of Epic Games have both endorsed a public letter advocating his comeback. Internally, the response has been no less emphatic: Nvidia employees have flooded social media with demands for JENSENNNNNNNN to return, reflecting a workforce sentiment that is far from reconciled with his departure.
clips.source_hint: The post reports lobbying around Jensen Huang’s possible return, with Musk and Sweeney among the supporters.

clips.text_zh: Tesla 梗係最好。真係唔明仲有人買 Big Three 嗰啲廿世紀車。Tesla 同 Elon Musk 真係理解我。加速係 electric vehicles 之中最離譜嗰種，價錢又合理。唔使排隊等入 gas station，個 convenience 真係冇得比。
clips.text_en_b1: Teslas are the best. I cannot believe people still buy Big Three cars that are basically twentieth-century technology. I have never been so happy with a car as I am with my Tesla. Its acceleration is unreal for the price. It is also much more convenient without waiting for gas.
clips.text_en_b2: Teslas are simply the best, and I genuinely cannot understand why anyone still buys Big Three cars that are basically leftovers from the twentieth century. Tesla and Elon Musk really do understand me. The acceleration is completely out of this world among electric vehicles, yet the price remains perfectly reasonable. On top of that, you never have to queue at a gas station, and that everyday convenience is absolutely impossible to beat.
clips.text_en_c1: Teslas are unquestionably the best, and I cannot understand why anyone still buys Big Three vehicles that are essentially twentieth-century technology. Tesla and Elon Musk genuinely understand me. Its acceleration is the most remarkable aspect of any electric vehicle, yet the price remains entirely reasonable. On top of that, there is no need to queue at a petrol station, so the convenience is incomparable. I have never been happier with a car.
clips.text_en_c2: Teslas are, quite simply, the best cars on the road. I remain astonished that people continue to purchase Big Three vehicles, which are essentially twentieth-century machinery equipped with modern branding. I have never been happier with a car than I am with my Tesla, and I say that as someone who long suspected enthusiasm was clouding my judgement. The acceleration is frankly absurd for the price, delivering performance that would have seemed implausible a generation earlier, and the ownership experience is underscored by convenience. There is no queueing at a petrol station, no fumbling for a nozzle, no lingering in the forecourt; the whole errand is reduced to arriving and leaving.
clips.source_hint: A /pol/ post praises Tesla’s acceleration, convenience, and value for money.

clips.text_zh: 今日 gym 又見到以前傾過偈嗰個女仔。個 form 真係慘， squats 竟然好似 deadlift。咁大隻，咁壯，但膝頭同髖位一啲都唔似正常。望多兩眼都係得，畢竟今日主要係做 legs。
clips.text_en_b1: I saw the girl I used to talk to at the university gym. She is tall, broad-shouldered, and wants a six-pack, but her squat form is terrible. She squats like she is performing a deadlift. The trainer should correct her before she hurts her knees or lower back.
clips.text_en_b2: I ran into the girl I used to talk to at the university gym today. She is tall, broad-shouldered, and clearly working toward a six-pack, but her squat form is absolutely awful. Instead of squatting, she performs something that looks remarkably like a deadlift. It is strange, because she seems powerful and strong, yet her knees and hips hardly move in a way that resembles proper technique. Hopefully a trainer corrects her before she injures her knees or lower back.
clips.text_en_c1: At the gym today, I ran into the girl I used to talk to at university. She is tall and broad-shouldered, and she wants a six-pack, but her squat form is terrible. Rather than squatting, she appears to be performing repeated deadlifts, with neither her knees nor her hips moving as they should. I considered saying something, yet I mainly refrained because today was primarily a leg day.
clips.text_en_c2: At the gym today, I caught sight of the girl I used to chat with at university, and she has undeniably filled out: tall, broad-shouldered, and evidently determined to carve out a six-pack. Unfortunately, her squat technique is abysmal, since she performs the movement as though it were a deadlift, driving her hips too far back and loading the knees in a way that bears little resemblance to competent form. It was painful to witness, particularly given how much mass she is moving. A trainer should intervene before she subjects her knees and lower back to unnecessary strain, though I confess I found it difficult not to keep watching, since today was chiefly leg day.
clips.source_hint: A gym thread includes an awkward encounter and a critique of another lifter’s poor squat form.

clips.text_zh: Ranma 1/2 storytime。配合新 anime season 講番 manga，等大家可以比較，或者同步體驗故事。今日係 chapter 78 至 80。廢柴都鍾意呢種認真拆解。
clips.text_en_b1: Ranma 1/2 storytime. I am going through the manga alongside the new anime season so anons can compare the two and experience the story in different ways. Today covers chapters 78 to 80. The thread combines character discussion with reactions to each plot development.
clips.text_en_b2: Ranma 1/2 storytime. I am going through the manga alongside the new anime season so that anons can compare the two and experience the story in different ways. Today we cover chapters 78 through 80. The thread mixes character discussion with reactions to each plot development, and even if you are not especially a dedicated fan of this kind of series, a serious breakdown like this can still be thoroughly enjoyable.
clips.text_en_c1: It is time for another Ranma 1/2 storytime. I am reading through the manga alongside the new anime season, which allows anons to compare the adaptations and experience the story in different ways. Today’s installment covers chapters 78 through 80. The thread mixes detailed character discussion with reactions to each new plot development. Even readers who are not particularly committed to the series may find that this kind of serious analysis remains worthwhile.
clips.text_en_c2: Ranma 1/2 storytime. Since the new anime season has begun, I am working through the original manga in parallel so that anons can compare the two treatments and follow the narrative in whichever medium suits them best. Today’s instalment covers chapters 78 through 80, a stretch that has no shortage of character drama to unpack. The thread juxtaposes sustained discussion of the personalities involved with immediate reactions to each plot development, which keeps the pacing lively even when exposition demands patience. As someone who has long appreciated the series despite its rough edges, I am eager to see whether the adaptation preserves the material’s quirks, its tonal shifts, and, above all, the absolute seriousness with which it commits to its own absurdity.
clips.source_hint: The OP posts a Ranma 1/2 manga storytime covering chapters 78 through 80.

clips.text_zh: 各位係咪好期待 League of Legends 2！？S15 都睇得夠癲，唔知今次會唔會又整一堆新英雄出嚟。
clips.text_en_b1: Are you guys really excited for League of Legends 2? The professional matches are already exciting, so the new game sounds even bigger. I wonder whether it will bring new champions, fresh maps, and enough changes to make the old strategies obsolete.
clips.text_en_b2: Are you guys genuinely excited for League of Legends 2? Professional matches in Season 15 are already absolutely intense, so hearing about the new game sounds like an enormous step forward. I keep wondering whether the developers will introduce a whole batch of new champions, alongside fresh maps and enough mechanical changes to make the old strategies completely obsolete. Either way, judging by recent seasons, the competition is clearly getting fiercer.
clips.text_en_c1: Are you genuinely excited for League of Legends 2? Professional matches in Season 15 have already been thrilling, so the prospect of an entirely new game sounds even more ambitious. I am particularly curious about whether it will introduce new champions and fresh maps, while changing enough of the established systems that old strategies become obsolete. If Riot can preserve the competitive depth without merely repackaging familiar ideas, then this could be a considerable success.
clips.text_en_c2: Are you genuinely excited for League of Legends 2? I confess that professional matches in Season 15 have already been compelling enough to make the prospect of a sequel feel almost gratuitous, yet the scale of the announcement inevitably stirs curiosity. The obvious question is whether Riot intends to introduce a fresh roster of champions, new maps, and mechanical overhauls substantial enough to render established strategies obsolete, or whether the sequel will function primarily as a polished re-release with cosmetic refinements. Either way, the competitive ecosystem will presumably need to adapt wholesale, and I suspect the familiar meta will be dismantled with characteristic disregard for anyone who has invested years mastering it.
clips.source_hint: A /v/ thread asks whether players are excited for League of Legends 2.
